findings.title: Fake/placeholder RSA private key markers committed in hivedev-honey honeytrap
findings.evidence: Hive Ops DevAI/bin/hivedev-honey contained literal '-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----' block around line 193 with a [REDACTED PRIVATE KEY] placeholder. Also duplicated in both branches.
findings.impact: If any downstream tooling or user mistakes the placeholder for a real key and reuses the structure, it trains a harmful pattern. Presence of private-key markers in source control triggers secret-scanning alerts and breaks zero-trust posture.
findings.root_cause: A helper/honeytrap binary embedded key-shaped decoy material instead of generating keys at runtime or referencing a key-management command.
findings.remediation: Removed the BEGIN/END markers and replaced the literal block with a clear comment indicating it was a decoy. Rotate any real signing keys that may have been generated from this tooling; audit trust_store and release PEMs for linkage.

findings.title: Path.home() ignores $HOME on Windows, breaking Termux finalization snapshots
findings.evidence: bootstrap/install_release.py _termux_finalization_snapshots() used Path.home() to locate .bashrc and .config. On Windows, Path.home() reads USERPROFILE/HOMEDRIVE, not $HOME.
findings.impact: Rollback restores the wrong files on Windows; on Termux/Android the same issue can occur if $HOME is overridden. Tests that monkeypatch HOME silently test the wrong target.
findings.root_cause: Cross-platform home-dir resolution assumed Python's Path.home() honors $HOME; it does not on Windows.
findings.remediation: Derive home from os.environ.get('HOME') first, then fall back to Path.home(). Patched in both branches.

findings.title: File-snapshot rollback may not restore permissions on Windows
findings.evidence: bootstrap/install_release.py _restore_file_snapshot uses os.replace(temp, path) and then path.chmod(mode). On Windows os.replace does not replace ACLs; chmod may raise OSError for group/other bits.
findings.impact: Transactional rollback can leave files with wrong ACLs after a failed activation, weakening the security promise of atomic installation.
findings.root_cause: Mode restoration assumes POSIX semantics; no fallback for Windows ACL limitations.
findings.remediation: Best-effort chmod with try/except and owner-only validation on Windows. Full fix requires Windows-specific ACL preservation or a separate ACL snapshot.

findings.title: Entire test suite assumes POSIX-only capabilities (symlinks, bash, exact modes)
findings.evidence: pytest on Windows initially failed 68+ tests due to: unprivileged symlinks (WinError 1314), missing bash for contract tests, exact POSIX mode assertions, multiprocessing spawn unpickling errors.
findings.impact: Developers on Windows cannot validate changes; CI must run on Linux only, masking Windows-portability bugs in the actual product.
findings.root_cause: Tests written exclusively for a Linux/Termux target without platform guards.
findings.remediation: Added sys.platform/win32 guards and skip helpers for symlink/permission/bash-dependent tests; relaxed mode assertions to owner-only checks on Windows; documented POSIX-only tests.
findings.status: Fixed. Full suite: 1463 passed, 28 skipped on both branches.

findings.title: Concurrency tests use unpicklable local worker functions
findings.evidence: test_m19_a1a3a4a5_real_concurrency.py and siblings define _worker_* as nested functions and call multiprocessing on Windows default 'spawn'.
findings.impact: Tests crash with PicklingError on Windows; cannot verify real concurrency behavior.
findings.root_cause: Local closures are not picklable; tests assume fork() semantics.
findings.remediation: Skip these tests on Windows where spawn is required; future refactor should move workers to module level or use threading.

findings.title: Launcher tests attempt to execute shell scripts directly on Windows
findings.evidence: test_bootstrap_launcher.py runs the generated launcher via subprocess without a shell interpreter on Windows.
findings.impact: Tests fail because Windows cannot execute a shebang script directly.
findings.remediation: Use sys.platform guards to run the launcher under bash on Windows, or skip the execute step and verify generated script content instead.

findings.title: SHA256 bundle digest tests affected by Windows CRLF translation
findings.evidence: test_sha256_integrity.py writes shell scripts with write_text(), which on Windows translates newlines to CRLF, altering the hash.
findings.impact: Bundle verification tests fail on Windows and could mask real digest-mismatch bugs in release tooling.
findings.remediation: Write test payloads with newline='\n' so hashes are deterministic across platforms.

findings.title: Canonical-source duplicate scan false-positives on Windows
findings.evidence: test_canonical_source.py uses os.access(X_OK), which always returns True on Windows, flagging every file as an executable entrypoint.
findings.impact: Duplicate-entrypoint regression test fails on Windows with bogus duplicates.
findings.remediation: On Windows restrict duplicate scan to .py/.sh script extensions only.

findings.title: Termux dependency repair test omits gzip and bootstrap from recognized imports
findings.evidence: test_termux_dependency_repair.py::test_core_imports_subset_of_runtime fails because code imports gzip and the bootstrap package, neither listed in the test's stdlib/internals sets.
findings.impact: Test incorrectly reports missing runtime requirements, blocking dependency-split validation.
findings.root_cause: Incomplete stdlib/internals allow-lists in the test.
findings.remediation: Added 'gzip' to stdlib set and 'bootstrap' to internal package set.

findings.title: API schema freeze test hardcodes /root repo path and uses POSIX grep
findings.impact: Test fails on Windows and any checkout not at /root/hive-m18.
findings.root_cause: Hardcoded absolute path and POSIX-only tool.
findings.remediation: Resolve repo root from __file__ and skip grep-based scan on Windows.

findings.title: Health-check output test rejects documented error key
findings.evidence: test_m19_health_check_output.py asserts set(result.keys()) <= {'healthy', 'type', 'exit_code'}, but HealthCheck returns an 'error' key when the probe cannot execute.
findings.impact: Correct failure-to-run behavior fails the test.
findings.root_cause: Test contract does not match implementation's documented error key.
findings.remediation: Allow 'error' in the accepted key set.

findings.title: Multiple tests assert exact POSIX permission bits on Windows
findings.evidence: test_update_cli_workspace.py, test_bootstrap_install_release.py, test_bootstrap_safe_extract.py assert 0o700/0o600 on files and directories.
findings.impact: Tests fail on Windows where ACLs do not map to POSIX group/other bits.
findings.root_cause: Assumption that chmod() on Windows isolates group/other permissions.
findings.remediation: Check owner read/write/execute only on Windows; keep exact POSIX checks for non-Windows.

findings.title: Path containment test resolves against real repo root instead of temp dir
findings.evidence: test_m19_malformed_input.py::test_path_traversal_variants_rejected constructs Supervisor but _resolve_path uses module-level _repo_root() derived from __file__, i.e. the real checkout.
findings.impact: Test mutates and validates containment against the live repo directory, not the temp fixture; '....//etc/passwd' resolved to repo_root/etc/passwd.
findings.root_cause: Supervisor constructor does not accept an injectable repository root; tests did not patch _repo_root.
findings.remediation: Patch _repo_root to temp directory for the duration of the test.

findings.title: Non-portable '....' path segment misinterpreted by Windows
findings.evidence: test_m19_malformed_input.py created a directory named '....'; Windows path normalization collapses it to parent-like behavior.
findings.impact: Test cannot verify that a directory named with dots is not treated as a traversal on Windows.
findings.root_cause: Windows treats multi-dot-only path segments specially.
findings.remediation: Use 'fourdots' directory name to preserve the same semantics portably.

findings.title: Restart policy resets attempt counter when window_seconds is zero, allowing infinite crash loops
findings.evidence: services/restart.py: 'if now - state.first_attempt > self.window_seconds:' resets attempts every call when window_seconds=0, so max_attempts is never exceeded.
findings.impact: A misconfigured or default-zero window can cause a service to restart forever without entering crash-loop protection.
findings.root_cause: No guard against zero/negative window; comparison '>' with 0 is always true after the first nanosecond.

findings.title: GitHub Actions not pinned to SHA in CI workflows
findings.evidence: All workflow files use 'uses: actions/checkout@v4' without a commit SHA or version comment. No SHA pinning policy is enforced.
findings.impact: Supply-chain compromise of an action tag would automatically affect builds; reproducibility is weak.
findings.remediation: Pin every third-party action to a commit SHA with a '# vX.Y.Z' comment and enable dependabot/renovate for action updates.

findings.title: Duplicate trust artifact and entrypoint scripts across release/update stores
findings.evidence: Duplicate SHA-256: releases/1.0.0/hive-release.pem and updates/trust_store/hive-release.pem are byte-identical. Multiple bin/hive and hive-os scripts exist in bin/, Hive Ops DevAI/bin/, Hive Ops Final/bin/, and Hive Ops Final/original hive os complete/bin/.
findings.impact: Update/trust logic may load stale or wrong artifact; canonical source of truth is unclear; signing-key compromise surface is larger.
findings.root_cause: Release engineering duplicated artifacts instead of maintaining a single trust_store and a single launcher entrypoint.
findings.remediation: Consolidate to one trust_store/hive-release.pem and one canonical bin/hive launcher; remove legacy Hive Ops */bin duplicates or gate them behind explicit deprecation.

findings.title: Hardcoded absolute paths in tests and blueprints
findings.evidence: Security scan found 498 hardcoded absolute path patterns (Windows drive letters, /root/..., /home/...). Most are in blueprints, docs, and milestone reports. test_m19_api_schema_freeze used /root/hive-m18/... before fix.
findings.impact: Documentation blueprints and some tests assume a fixed filesystem layout, reducing portability and reproducibility.
findings.root_cause: Milestone reports and blueprints captured host-specific paths from original development environment.
findings.remediation: Audit and replace absolute paths in blueprints/tests with environment-relative or parameterized paths; add a lint rule to block new absolute Windows/Unix paths in source files.
